digest.lead: Anthropic pushed another incremental Claude Code update (v2.1.210) focused on reliability fixes — worktree isolation bugs and permission-rule clarity — while on the product side it announced Claude For Teachers, extending its education push alongside a new Canadian AI research initiative.
digest.summary: The developer community continues to build on top of Claude: a new open-source GUI coding agent (Juggler) and a Dropbox-based skill-sharing tool (Sx 2.0) both drew strong Hacker News engagement, alongside a YC-backed startup extracting feedback from agent conversations.

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude For Teachers
stories.summary: Anthropic introduced Claude For Teachers, a new offering aimed at bringing Claude's capabilities into classrooms and educator workflows [1].
stories.impact: Signals Anthropic's continued push into education-specific products, targeting teachers and schools as a distinct user segment.

stories.headline: Anthropic Announces Canadian AI Research Initiative
stories.summary: Anthropic published details of a new research effort focused on AI in Canada, marking an expansion of its research and policy engagement in the region [1].
stories.impact: Reflects Anthropic's broader strategy of deepening international research partnerships and regional presence outside the US.

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.210 Fixes Worktree Isolation Bug, Adds Elapsed-Time Indicator
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code release adds a live elapsed-time counter to long-running tool calls so they no longer appear stuck, and warns users at startup if they've set overly broad permission rules like `Write(path)` instead of the safer `Edit(path)` [1]. It also fixes a bug where subagents running in isolated worktrees could still mutate the main repo's git checkout, and patches an issue where the `ultracode` keyword could be triggered by non-human input [1].
key_points: Live elapsed-time counter added to collapsed tool summary lines for long-running calls [1]
Startup warnings now flag risky permission rules such as `Write(path)`, `NotebookEdit(path)`, and `Glob(path)` [1]
Fixed worktree-isolated subagents incorrectly running git-mutating commands against the main repo [1]
stories.impact: The worktree isolation fix matters most for developers running parallel subagents, preventing accidental corruption of the main repository checkout during isolated tasks.

stories.headline: Open-Source GUI Coding Agent 'Juggler' Draws Strong HN Engagement
stories.summary: Juggler, an open-source GUI coding agent built by the creator of JUCE, launched on Hacker News and drew 230 points and over 100 comments [1]. The tool positions itself as a graphical alternative to terminal-based coding agents like Claude Code.
stories.impact: Highlights growing developer interest in GUI-based alternatives to CLI coding agents, potentially broadening the audience for agentic coding tools beyond terminal-comfortable developers.

sources.title: Show HN: Juggler – an open-source GUI coding agent, by the creator of JUCE

stories.headline: Sx 2.0 Lets Teams Share AI Skills Through a Dropbox Folder
stories.summary: Sx 2.0 launched on Hacker News, offering a lightweight way for teams to share AI agent skills using a simple Dropbox folder as a 'skill server' [1]. The launch generated 43 points and 33 comments from developers interested in low-friction skill distribution.
stories.impact: Offers a simple, infrastructure-free way for teams using Claude and similar agents to distribute reusable skills, appealing to small teams wary of heavier tooling.

sources.title: Show HN: Sx 2.0 – Share AI skills with your team through a Dropbox folder

stories.headline: YC-Backed Agnost AI Extracts User Feedback From Agent Conversations
stories.summary: Agnost AI, part of YC's S26 batch, launched on Hacker News with a tool that extracts structured user feedback from conversations with AI agents [1]. The launch received 77 points and 40 comments.
stories.impact: Relevant to teams building products on top of Claude and other agent frameworks who need systematic ways to turn chat logs into actionable product feedback.

sources.title: Launch HN: Agnost AI (YC S26) – Extract user feedback from agent conversations

stories.headline: Configure worktree base reference to preserve unpushed commits
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code update changed the default behavior for worktrees to branch from origin instead of local HEAD, potentially losing unpushed commits. Setting the baseRef to 'head' preserves your local work when creating new worktrees.

stories.headline: Use the Dynamic Workflow Size setting to control agent counts
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.202 adds a 'Dynamic workflow size' option in /config that lets you guide how many agents Claude spawns for dynamic workflows (small/medium/large). This is an advisory setting, not a hard cap, so it helps balance speed vs. thoroughness for multi-agent tasks.
actionable_steps: Set it to small, medium, or large based on task complexity and desired agent count

stories.headline: Enable Amazon Bedrock support with Mantle integration
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.94 added support for Amazon Bedrock through Mantle integration. This allows you to use Claude Code with Amazon's Bedrock service instead of the default API endpoints, potentially offering better performance or compliance for enterprise users.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE=1 in your system or terminal
Restart Claude Code to apply the new configuration
Verify the connection is working by running a test query

stories.headline: Configure streaming timeout for better connection handling
stories.summary: The new CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable lets you customize how long Claude Code waits before timing out idle streaming connections. This helps prevent unnecessary disconnections during long-running operations.
actionable_steps: Choose a timeout value in milliseconds (default is 90000 for 90 seconds)
Restart Claude Code for the setting to take effect

stories.headline: Organize project rules using .claude/rules/ directory structure
stories.summary: The .claude/rules/ directory lets you break down complex project instructions into organized, manageable files. This makes it easier to maintain large codebases and share specific rules across multiple projects.
actionable_steps: Create a .claude/rules/ directory in your project root
Split your CLAUDE.md instructions into focused rule files (e.g., coding-style.md, testing.md)
Use symlinks to share common rules across multiple projects
Reference rule files from your main CLAUDE.md using import statements
